title: Symmetrization preserves average cost
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube ${\pm1}^n$, and let $T$ be a randomized decision tree computing $f$ whose input and output alphabets are ${\pm1}$. For any probability distribution $pi$ on ${\pm1}$, the average cost of the symmetrized tree under the independent product input distribution equals the average cost of $T$ under that distribution.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
$T$ computes $f$ and has sign-valued inputs and outputs
$T$ has a finite nonempty seed space and seed probability law
$pi$ is a probability distribution on the sign alphabet
